title: RoboParty launches open-source RP1 humanoid robot
key_facts: RoboParty launched RP1 (ROBOTO 01), a full-stack open-source humanoid robot for robotics research and embodied AI (AI that controls a physical body).
Hardware designs, the RoboParty-made ROMOMO joint motors, low-level drivers, control code, simulation resources and software kits are opened to researchers.
The standard RP1 is about 1.3 meters tall with 24 actuated joints; the Pro version has 30, including a neck and two arms; the counts exclude the hands.
RP1 already supports walking, recovery from pushes, getting up after a fall and human motion tracking, according to the article.
Tools include virtual reality teleoperation, data collection and playback, motion retargeting and whole-body control.
RoboParty started the open-source RPO project in January 2026; it has more than 2,600 GitHub stars.
The text reads like a company release: no price, availability, customers or independent test is given.
quote_evidence: RoboParty officially launches RP1 (ROBOTO 01), a high-performance, full-stack open-source humanoid robot designed for advanced robotics research and embodied AI development.
The standard RP1 stands approximately 1.3 meters tall and features 24 actuated degrees of freedom (DoF), supporting research into gait, balance control and sim-to-real transfer.
RP1 already supports foundational motor capabilities, including continuous walking, recovery from external disturbances, getting back up after a fall and human motion tracking.
why_it_matters_hint: An open humanoid platform lets researchers inspect and change the robot itself, not just its software, but no price or independent test is given.
notes: The article reads like RoboParty's own release; all capabilities are company statements. No price, availability or outside test is stated.
